ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, B, and C are on the same straight line, and BD bisects $\angle ABE$, $\angle EBC=30^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle DBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle EBC=30^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle ABE=180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ$,\\
since BD bisects $\angle ABE$,\\
thus $\angle DBE= \frac{1}{2}\angle ABE=75^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle DBC=\angle DBE+\angle EBC=\boxed{105^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A, B, C lie on a horizontal straight line with rays BD and BE going upward from B, and BE is between BD and BC. Read from the text that BD bisects angle ABE and that angle EBC is 30°. Since AB and BC are opposite rays, angle ABC is a straight angle of 180°. Therefore angle ABE is the supplement of angle EBC: 180° - 30° = 150°. Because BD bisects angle ABE, angle DBE = 75°. Finally, from the image order of rays, angle DBC is made of angle DBE plus angle EBC, so 75° + 30° = 105°.
